module: Identify actors and design interaction disclosure

lesson.title: Agents, principals and human supervisors
lesson.summary: Distinguish statutory AI disclosure from guidance about represented principals and supervisory steps.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must allocate the relevant duty before choosing an implementation.
The learner must identify a direct human interaction before testing this disclosure rule.

blocks: An **AI agent** is an AI system that can carry out tasks, for example managing correspondence or making bookings. When it can interact with people, the Article 50(1) analysis applies.
Paragraph 31 of the Commission Guidelines explains how the interaction rule applies to agents. It is interpretative guidance, not three new numbered statutory duties.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(1); Commission Guidelines paragraph 31
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: The **principal** is the person or organisation on whose behalf the agent acts. The guidance says agents should disclose their artificial nature and that represented person, addressing origin, delegated authority and accountability.
A suitable Harbour message is: 'I am Harbour Services' AI booking assistant, acting for Harbour Services.' Saying only 'I am an assistant' can leave both artificial nature and representation unclear.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(1); Commission Guidelines paragraph 31
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: A provider may not know every later context where an agent reaches a person. The guidance advises architecture-level design and instructions to disclose wherever human interaction is reasonably likely.

Passing a task through another agent does not remove the need to consider the final human contact. Use a disclosure route that survives the actual handoff rather than assuming all later exchanges are machine-only.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(1); Commission Guidelines paragraph 31
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: The guidance also addresses the **instructing or supervising person**. The agent should disclose itself at authorisation, reporting and validation steps, and at every new interaction.
This includes processing outputs from other AI systems. A report to a supervisor should not silently imply that an AI-generated result came directly from a person.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(1); Commission Guidelines paragraph 31
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

questions.prompt: Harbour's booking agent contacts a hotel. Which introduction follows the agent-specific Commission guidance?

options.blocks: That it is AI and acts for Harbour Services
options.reason: The guidance addresses artificial nature and represented principal.

options.blocks: Only that it is called Alex
options.reason: A name does not explain AI nature or representation.

options.blocks: Only that the booking concerns a hotel
options.reason: Task subject does not explain origin and authority.

variants.prompt: What should the hotel be told when Harbour's AI agent acts for Harbour?

options.blocks: Only that it is called Alex
options.reason: A name does not explain AI nature or representation.

options.blocks: Only that the booking concerns a hotel
options.reason: Task subject does not explain origin and authority.

options.blocks: That it is AI and acts for Harbour Services
options.reason: The guidance addresses artificial nature and represented principal.

questions.prompt: An agent sends its supervisor an AI-generated result obtained from another agent. What should its design account for?

options.blocks: Silence because only direct human input matters
options.reason: The guidance explicitly includes reliance on other AI outputs.

options.blocks: Disclosure only when the booking is completed
options.reason: Relevant authorisation and validation steps can occur earlier.

options.blocks: Disclosure to the instructing person at that key step
options.reason: Guideline paragraph 31 includes reporting and validation, including AI-sourced inputs.

variants.prompt: What matters at a supervisory validation step involving another agent's output?

options.blocks: Disclosure only when the booking is completed
options.reason: Relevant authorisation and validation steps can occur earlier.

options.blocks: Disclosure to the instructing person at that key step
options.reason: Guideline paragraph 31 includes reporting and validation, including AI-sourced inputs.

options.blocks: Silence because only direct human input matters
options.reason: The guidance explicitly includes reliance on other AI outputs.

questions.prompt: The provider cannot reliably predict whether a deployed agent will contact people. Which approach follows the guidance?

options.blocks: Treat the guidance as three new statutory paragraphs
options.reason: These are interpretations of Article 50(1), not separate enacted clauses.

options.blocks: Design disclosure into likely human-contact situations
options.reason: The guidance advises architecture-level design for that uncertainty.

options.blocks: Omit disclosure until every recipient is known
options.reason: That would leave reasonably likely human interactions uncovered.

options.reason: The guidance advises architecture-level design for that uncertainty.
